findings.observation: Both phone studies compress the filmstrip imagery into tiny dots and thin landscape bands. The selected interval is clear, but the pictured moments are indistinguishable.
findings.impact: Creators can read the trim numerically but cannot use the decisive filmstrip to recognize which footage they are keeping. Neither study fully resolves the task at phone size.
findings.repair: Use fewer, larger representative thumbnails with readable landscape detail at narrow widths. Preserve the interval, grips and readouts. Recheck at the delivered 390px width that temporal differences remain recognizable.

findings.observation: B’s desktop portrait crop cuts off the sun and removes much of the landscape context while allocating less width to the timeline.
findings.impact: The side-by-side arrangement sacrifices both source context and temporal inspection space without demonstrating a compensating task benefit.
findings.repair: Carry forward A’s preview-above-timeline arrangement and wider desktop filmstrip. Recheck it with the repaired phone thumbnails before expansion.

strengths: The studies materially compare the named composition decision: A prioritizes landscape context; B prioritizes controls and places a portrait-cropped preview beside them on desktop.
A provides the stronger visible task path across widths, keeping recognizable source imagery above clearly grouped trim controls.
Both use restrained, coherent editor styling. Amber grips and perimeter identify the kept interval, and prominent duration plus explicit endpoints make the current selection understandable.
The illustrated coastline is appropriate subject material for this fictional sample; additional decoration or a new identity is unnecessary.
limits: Inspected all four captures at native size in the requested order.
Still images do not verify dragging, touch targets, keyboard operation, focus, reset behavior, live preview updates or reduced motion.
The composition comparison supports choosing A as the repair base, but neither study is ready to expand without improving phone filmstrip readability.
